antagonists.rationale_text: Einstellung-effect undermines international-negotiation-and-diplomacy-models by causing practitioners to default to a familiar negotiation framework rather than diagnosing the actual structure of the current multi-party interaction.
antagonists.source_quote: The Hammer-in-Search-of-a-Nail (Maslow's Hammer): This pitfall occurs when practitioners rely unquestioningly on familiar conceptual frameworks, adopting the mental model of a function or industry with all its assumptions. This is dangerous when the underlying assumptions of the framework are not met.
antagonists.affinity_rationale: Decision-maker defaults to a simple model they know rather than understanding the complicated reality — causes incorrect framing and 'disastrously wrong solutions' in negotiation contexts.
antagonists.activation_condition: When negotiation strategy defaults to familiar frameworks rather than building context-specific understanding of the counterparty's actual reality and constraints

antagonists.rationale_text: Curse-of-knowledge undermines international-negotiation-and-diplomacy-models by causing experts to communicate strategy at a level of abstraction the counterparty or stakeholder cannot absorb, blocking the persuasion and influence the model requires.
antagonists.source_quote: The difficulty experts have in remembering what it is like not to know something. This impairs communication because the expert instinctively talks at a higher level of abstraction than the audience can absorb, leading to ineffective transfer of strategy.
antagonists.affinity_rationale: Expert difficulty remembering what it is like not to know something impairs communication — 'instinctively talks at a higher level of abstraction than the audience can absorb'.
antagonists.activation_condition: When diplomatic or negotiation communication fails because expert-level framing exceeds the counterparty's conceptual framework or knowledge base
